Q: Pygame 2D image animations rendering in the wrong way A:

As you can see, the flipping is working fine - What happens is that the base coordinate point, from which your character is drawn, are the coordinates that are on the top-left of your character image.

(sorry, reading your code -it is the point

So, when it is facing right, these are some point behind the character back, and the sword seems to point forward. When flipping the character, this point will be at the left at the sword tip - and the character body will appear to be pushed to the right by the length of the sword.

What you need to to is to add a negative offset of a few pixels to the character position when drawing it, which would compensate the sword length if it extends to the left.

You should put in your character (it can be in the init), a mapping of which frames, and which action, and which flip state, the offset should be - and then, upon drawing it, add that offset to the self.rect:

self.offsets = {}
# your current example will need this:
self.offsets["attack", 0, True] = pygame.Vector2(-10, 0) # trying 10 pixels here, you might want to fine tune this number
# Add other entries if needed
...

Eventually, you could put that data in a text file, alongside your code, and parse it when initializing the game: that would allow another person, designing the sprites, to input the correct offsets for you, without having to hardcode that in the the Python code.

And then, to use these offsets, at the animate method, bellow the match block you could add:

match self.animation_state:
    ...

self.rect.topleft += self.offsets.get(
        (self.animation_state, int(self.animation_index), self.flip),
         pygame.Vector2(0, 0)
    )

Q: pytest monkeypatch methods with return values from parametrized method A:

I'm unable to recreate the problem. Maybe a different code path is executed than what the monkeypatch attributes are set for.

In the below minimal example I added some of the complexity in your example: A class A in module a.py with the validate function to be patched:

class A:
    def validate(self):
        status, result = "not", "patched"
        return status, result

A class B in module b.py using functionality from class A in module a.py:

import a
class B():

    def build(self):
        return a.A().validate()

A test module test.py:

import pytest
from a import A
from b import B

@pytest.mark.parametrize("arg1, arg2", [("foo1", "bar1"), ("foo2", "bar2")])
def test_monkeypatch_with_params(monkeypatch, arg1, arg2):

    def validate(self):
        print(arg1, arg2)
        return arg1, arg2

    monkeypatch.setattr(A, "validate", validate)

    actual_status, actual_result = B().build()
    assert actual_status == arg1
    assert actual_result == arg2

executed as:

pytest test.py -s

Q: 2 Way data binding not working in ng-select Angular 6 A:

Use (change) event from html like below 

  <ng-select [items] = "arrobjCategories"  bindLabel = "name"
bindValue = "id" [(ngModel)] = "selectedProductCategoryId"
(change) = "onProductCategoryChange($event)"> </ng-select>
Use the change event in type script file like below

  public onProductCategoryChange(event){
    console.log(event);
  }

Here event will contain actual selected data.

Q: How to get x and y coordinates of image inside an imageview in android? A:

I don't really understand what you're asking, but I'll try to answer anyway. It sounds like you want to use getRawX() and getRawY() to get the touch position on the screen and not on the view. You may also have to override the onTouchEvent method for whatever is outside of the ImageView.

Q: Is there a Google Sheets formula to put the name of the sheet into a cell? A:

Not sure whether this option has been introduced only recently (it's undocumented), but there is a sheet parameter that can be passed on to the CELL() function. It returns the current sheet name! You can use it as follows:

=CELL("sheet", A1)
